title: Potain launches ECS a new era of smart, connected tower crane control for emerging markets
summary: Customizable control, intelligent data logging, and faster fault diagnosis define the new platform.The system harnesses CAN bus architecture for simpler and more reliable maintenance of Potain tower cranes.
body_markdown:
Behind the HMI, the Potain ECS harnesses Controller Area Network (CAN) bus architecture for simpler, more reliable maintenance. The easier layout uses just two wires to replace dozens that would typically connect the crane’s motors, sensors, and switches. It’s faster to install, lighter, more reliable, simpler to troubleshoot, and easy to expand and modify as new functionality is added.


Management of the ECS is controlled by either the operator or technician directly from the HMI. Details of the crane's status and performance are displayed on the HMI, showing wind speed, working radius, weight of the load, slewing angle, and more. It is connected to a central controller which connects via the CAN wiring to the slewing, hoisting, luffing, trolleying controls plus the control units, load sensors, and limiters/encoders.


Using the HMI, operators can switch between eight display screens that provide access to crane data, operating preferences, zoning functions, display settings and other key system information. Additional control modes are available for technicians and fleet administrators, with greater functionality.
